cvEn:
Shimon Nisani, son of Rachel and Mattityahu, was born on 26 September 1922, the 4th of Tishrei 5683, in the town of Hamadan, Persia. In 1925 he immigrated to the Land of Israel with his family. When he was five years old he was orphaned of his father, and from the age of ten he grew up and was educated at the Diskin Orphanage in Jerusalem.

He was a carpenter and opened his own carpentry workshop. He was pleasant in manner and easy to get along with.

As a member of the Haganah, he was among the first to answer the call-up after the UN General Assembly decision of 29 November 1947 on the partition of the country. He served on guard duty at a post in the Mandelbaum Houses in the Hungarian Quarter. While on duty near the Mustara neighborhood on 2 Adar I 5708, 12 February 1948, he was arrested by the British together with four of his comrades. Near the Lions' Gate, the British handed them over to an Arab mob, which murdered the four. He was buried on the Mount of Olives in Jerusalem. His name is inscribed on the memorial erected at the Military Cemetery on Mount Herzl in memory of the fallen of the Jewish Quarter and of the fighters who fell in the battle for Jerusalem and were buried on the Mount of Olives.
